Donald Trump once boasted on social media that Chinese President Xi Jinping would offer him a "big, fat hug" ahead of his upcoming trip to China.

However, Beijing's extensive economic ties to Iran, alongside persistent trade tensions stemming from Mr Trump's first term, threaten to dampen any anticipated warmth when he arrives this week.

This comes despite Mr Trump's long-standing praise for Mr Xi, whom he views as a formidable leader deserving of his respect.

Known for his aversion to lengthy travel, Mr Trump is expected to spend only parts of three days on Chinese soil.

While some ceremonial grandeur is anticipated, the visit is unlikely to replicate the lavish "state visit-plus" reception Beijing afforded him in 2017.

Jonathan Czin, a former director for China at the National Security Council during the Biden administration, observed: "Even before this whole conflagration with Iran, they weren’t going to go state visit-plus like last time, just because things are tense".

That earlier trip saw China extend a full red-carpet welcome, complete with military music, flag-waving children, and chants of "Welcome".

open image in gallery On Trump's first-term trip, China rolled out the red carpet for his arrival, with a band playing military music and children waving flags and chanting ‘Welcome’ ( AFP/Getty )

Xi offered a tour of the Forbidden City. Trump and first lady Melania Trump even had a private dinner there. Trump was the first foreign leader since the People’s Republic of China was founded in 1949 to experience what was once reserved for emperors.

The following morning brought another welcome ceremony at the Great Hall of the People and featured a military parade. There also was a state banquet in Trump’s honor with video highlights from the Chinese leader’s previous visit to Florida and a clip of Trump’s granddaughter Arabella singing in Chinese.

Beijing does not offer this level of spectacle to most visiting foreign leaders. When British Prime Minister Keir Starmer visited the Forbidden City in January, Xi did not attend and the site remained open to the public. Starmer had to contend with tourists.

Ali Wyne, senior U.S.-China research and advocacy adviser for the Washington nonprofit the Crisis Group, said the “Chinese delegation will likely do its utmost to ensure that Trump leaves Beijing believing that he has just concluded the most extraordinary state visit of his two presidencies”.

But, he said, the “pomp and circumstance would serve a different role now than they did when he first visited Beijing” because “Xi has a much better understanding of Trump, and the administration’s own national security strategy and national defense strategy recognize China as a near-peer”.

open image in gallery After his visit to Beijing, Trump plans to host Xi at the White House ( AP )

Expectations for what gets accomplished could be lower this time, said Czin, now a fellow at the Brookings Institution.

He predicted that the Chinese may not offer major breakthroughs on trade or anything else because they are “working backward from our midterm elections” with the theory that the closer they get to Election Day “the more leverage they are going to have”.

The GOP is focused on retaining control of Congress, even as polling shows most Americans are unhappy with Trump’s economic policies and believe that the United States went too far in Iran. Still, the White House argues that Trump's previous firm hand with Beijing on tariffs — which the Supreme Court subsequently struck down — means the U.S. will remain in a strong position.

“President Trump cares about results, not symbols" White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said. “But even still, the president has a great relationship with President Xi, and the upcoming summit in Beijing will be both symbolically and substantively significant”.

Trump could meet with China's leader four times in eight months.

After his visit to Beijing, Trump plans to host Xi at the White House. Trump might also attend the November Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in Shenzhen, China. And Xi could come to the Group of 20 summit the following month at Trump’s resort in Doral, Florida.

Czin noted that Xi also is not very fond of travel, meaning not all of the planned encounters may happen. He said China's leader also does not “do personal connections" like the kind Trump relishes, noting Xi led a Chinese military purge in January that included replacing officials with long-standing personal ties to his family.

open image in gallery Trump could potentially meet with President Xi four times in eight months ( AFP/Getty )

Wyne, though, said Xi also “appreciates that he is unlikely to deal with another U.S. president who admires him as greatly and embraces as narrow a view of strategic competition.”

That means Xi may "attempt to pocket as many economic and security concessions from Trump as possible,” Wyne said.

Trump told The Wall Street Journal's editorial board in 2024 that Xi “was actually a really good ... I don’t want to say ‘friend’. I don’t want to act foolish. ‘He was my friend’. But I got along with him great”.

Trump even suggested at the time that military force might not be required to ensure that Chinese troops do not encroach on Taiwan, simply because China’s leader "respects me” despite Trump more recently discussing potentially selling arms to Taiwan.

Trump has continued to praise the bilateral relationship since returning to the White House, even after his Beijing visit, originally scheduled for March, was postponed due to the early stages of the Iran war.

He unsuccessfully prodded China to get involved in reopening the Strait of Hormuz after Iranian forces choked it off and disrupted global economies. But China did use its leverage as the largest purchaser of Iranian oil to encourage Iran to agree to what has been a fragile ceasefire.

open image in gallery TRUMP-CHINA ( AP )

Beijing has strong economic ties to Tehran, and the war could hurt its economy, which was already projected to grow more slowly. If China can help establish lasting peace, though, that might boost its standing in negotiations on trade issues with the Trump administration.

During his 2017 visit, Trump announced $250 billion in nonbinding trade deals, some of which never materialized. A round of trade deals announced in 2020 and worth $200 billion mostly never came to fruition before Trump's first term ended.

More recently, Trump’s announcement last year of steep global tariffs prompted China to cut off purchases of U.S. soybeans and clamp down on exports of rare earth minerals needed by American factories.

Tensions have eased somewhat since the U.S. reached a trade truce last fall that has limited tariffs on both sides. The administration has continued to make reducing the U.S. trade deficit with China a priority, insisting it can do so while still working to encourage trade between the two countries.

“I expect great stability in the relationship," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said. "But that doesn’t mean our trade deficit can’t continue dropping”.

Kelly, the White House spokeswoman, said Trump “doesn’t travel anywhere without bringing deliverables home to our country".

"Americans can expect the president to deliver more good deals for the United States while in China” she said.

News.title: Anderson justifies £100m valuation and puts Forest on brink of safety
News.content:
In the last two Premier League seasons, 30 points would have been enough to avoid relegation. This year, even 40 may be insufficient. Nottingham Forest are one of England’s form teams and sit on 42 points with three games to play – but they still need three more points to be sure of survival.

Forest have a vastly superior goal difference to West Ham, who could potentially reach 45 points. That may change after West Ham face Arsenal later today. All Forest can do is control the controllables: if they win at home to Newcastle, they will effectively – if not mathematically – be safe.

Forest’s brilliant start under Vitor Pereira came to a juddering halt at Villa Park on Thursday, when they were thrashed by Aston Villa in the Europa League semi-final second leg. “It’s difficult today but tomorrow is another day,” said Pereira in his pre-match press conference. “We need to compete against Newcastle – it’s a very important game in the relegation battle – and, especially mentally, we need to come back.”

It’s likely that Forest will again be without the influential Morgan Gibbs-White, who was an unused substitute against Villa after suffering a facial injury in the league win at Chelsea on Monday.

Victory today would lift Forest above Newcastle, yet the middle of the table is so congested that Newcastle – who start the day in 13th – could still qualify for Europe.

“We’re looking to try and win our last three games,” said Eddie Howe. “All our energy is going into that. The lads have been focused this week. There’s been no end-of-season feel to our training ground work, that’s really important. While there’s still an opportunity, we’ll try and grab it.”

Kick off 2pm

News.title: Challenge Starmer or I will, Labour MP tells Cabinet
News.content:
A Labour MP has told Cabinet ministers to challenge Sir Keir Starmer or she will trigger a leadership contest herself.

Catherine West, the MP for Hornsey and Friern Barnet and a former foreign minister, said she had put the Cabinet “on notice” until Monday, by which time she will ask MPs to back her in triggering a contest.

The Prime Minister is facing growing calls for his resignation after leading his party to its worst local election results on Thursday.

Ms West told BBC Radio 4: “My preferred option is for the Cabinet to do a reshuffle within itself, where there’s plenty of talent, and for Keir to be given a different role, which he might enjoy, perhaps an international role.

“Then for others to come to the fore who can communicate the message, who are very able, so we can have minimum fuss.”

More than 30 Labour MPs have broken ranks to demand the Prime Minister set out a timeline for his departure following sweeping losses across England, Scotland and Wales.

Sir Keir said that while the results had been “really tough”, he would not stand down, adding that he would set out a message of “hope for the future” in the coming days. A reset speech is expected as soon as Monday.

For a leadership election to start, a minimum of 81 Labour MPs would have to back a single challenger.

One Labour MP from the moderate wing of the party described Ms West as a “hero”.

They said: “Hopefully this will kick the cabinet into doing the right thing – to go to the PM and tell him the time is up. The vast majority of MPs are just unbelievably frustrated with the fact that the Cabinet are refusing to come to terms with reality and can’t see the writing on the wall.”

They added that they would be “shocked” if Ms West failed to get to the 81 backers needed. They said this would begin with those on the Left of the party, but following Sir Keir’s reset speech on Monday, moderates would start to add their names too.

However, allies of Andy Burnham, widely tipped as a future leader, are trying to convince Ms West to abandon her own run.The Telegraph has been told that Louise Haigh, who called for Sir Keir to resign yesterday, and members of the soft-Left Tribune group, are trying to work out how to stop Ms West from running.

They are concerned that if a leadership contest is triggered now, Mr Burnham will not be eligible to run because he is not an MP.

Ms West was first elected to her constituency in May 2015. She served as a minister in the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office until Sir Keir removed her from the post in September 2025.

A government source said that she had issued her ultimatum to the Cabinet because she was disgruntled after her sacking by Sir Keir.

They told The Telegraph: “He sacked her and now she wants to sack him.”

News.title: ‘Come on you Irons!’: Guardiola turns West Ham fan as Man City keep title race alive
News.content:
Manchester City host Brentford at the Etihad Stadium, knowing a win is an absolute non-negotiable to stay in the title race. Their title hopes took a major hit on Monday night as they drew 3-3 at Everton. They had led that game 1-0 but a mad quarter of an hour in the second half saw them fall 3-1 down only to score two late goals to draw, including a 97th-minute equaliser from Jeremy Doku. Pep Guardiola has hailed the form of the Belgian winger.

“I am so glad,” Guardiola said. “I am so glad they are making the step and feel that the winger had to score and make an impact not just an extra one against one. The goals, the assists, also contributing defensively; Jeremy has been amazing this season. Amazing.”

This weekend Manchester City get to play before their title rivals Arsenal and have the opportunity to cut the gap to two points ahead of Arsenal’s game at West Ham on Sunday. The hosts could welcome Rodri back, with the Spaniard having missed their last three games. Josko Gvardiol and Ruben Dias are nearing returns to fitness.

Brentford come into this game off the back of a 3-0 home win over West Ham last weekend. Keith Andrews’ side are firmly in the race for European football. There were doubts about Andrews replacing Frank last summer but the Irishman has led them to seventh place going into the final three games of the season.

“The narrative around last week’s game was all around West Ham and the fight to stay in the league,” Keith Andrews told Sky Sports. “I was pretty firm then that I do not really care about that, to be blunt. I care about us and what we are trying to do and it is similar this weekend. I obviously know the effect that it can have, the result whichever way it goes, but we have got our own agenda to take care of. The edge that we play with I really, really like. I like watching us. I really like watching us.

“We are a team that respects the opposition, respects the level, respects what you need to do to get results in the league. But equally we have this feel of we will go toe-to-toe with any team in the league. We are in a decent run of form. We are playing pretty well. We are still playing with a lot of energy and personality, which I like.”

Having missed the last four matches with injury, Jordan Henderson is back available for the visitors.

Manchester City won the reverse fixture 1-0 at the Gtech Stadium back in October, with Erling Haaland scoring the only goal of the game. These sides also met in the League Cup in December, with Manchester City winning 2-0 at the Etihad.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Leicester give Northampton ‘painful thumping’ in feisty East Midlands derby
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live blog for this Gallagher Prem meeting and East Midlands Derby between Leicester Tigers and Northampton Saints.

With just four games of the regular campaign remaining before the play-offs, the Prem is shaping up for a dramatic finale as we approach the deciding weeks of a fascinating season. Northampton are leading the pack, but are just four points ahead of second-place Bath, who they beat 41-38 in an enthralling encounter at Franklin’s Gardens last time out. Meanwhile, Leicester, who sit third, narrowly lost 19-15 to Saracens in their previous outing, falling 10 points behind the league leaders.

Two weeks ago, Northampton were drawing 38-all with Bath, before Enoch Opuku-Gyamfi’s high tackle on Henry Pollock gifted Fin Smith a penalty, which the Englishman slotted between the posts in the 83rd minute, sealing an extra three points and the win.

Phil Dowson, Northampton’s director of rugby, was pleased with the result, but was unhappy with its chaotic nature. “We are top of the table, having lost once this season, so let’s not get too carried away with this game of rugby. But, fundamentally, this game of rugby was not good enough and it could have been a second loss. Delighted with the win but very disappointed by the performance. Lee Radford [defence coach] is particularly annoyed. Rugby is supposed to be fun – an underrated word – but we cannot rely on the Harlem Globetrotters stuff to get us out of trouble.”

Leicester’s disappointing defeat against a Noah Caluori-inspired Saracens was a blow to their play-off ambitions, with Geoff Parling’s men sitting just four points ahead of fifth-place Bristol Bears. Leicester have already scooped the Prem Rugby Cup thanks to a dominant 66-14 victory over Exeter Chiefs back in March, and will want to cement their place in the top four to ensure they qualify for the play-offs. More domestic success could be on the horizon for Leicester, who will be aiming to spoil Northampton’s party.

Kick-off from Mattioli Wood Welford Road is at 15.05pm.

News.title: Marlie Packer scores four but England’s defence raises concern ahead of Grand Slam decider
News.content:
Packer, 36, who made her debut in the same back row as another legendary England openside flanker, Maggie Alphonsi, and has now created her own legacy in the No 7 shirt, is the experienced head and highlighted the work that needs to be done this week.

“We need to be a bit better,” said Packer. “We need to be more ‘see, do’. We are thinking, and as soon as you think the other team’s got a foot on top of you. We’re thinking a little bit too much, and actually just trust the process, trust what we’re trying to do. There is a little bit of mentality, bit of mindset in there.

“The defensive maul was an issue in the Wales game, that last try they scored against us, and then obviously for it to happen again against Italy, it’s not something we pride ourselves on at all,” said Packer, who has now scored 59 tries for her country, just two behind Sue Day’s record.

“It’d be something that we massively probably talk about this week. A lot of the players that were on the pitch at the time, it was their first cap in a Red Roses shirt. So actually, it’s a learning for them… they’ll watch it back, we will work out where we went wrong, but we can’t let that happen against France.”

Yet on this form, it seems that yet another clean sweep will be a procession. As Mitchell quipped when asked about his side’s defensive work-ons, he said: “We will just score more.”

The most impressive aspect of England’s campaign is that they have not missed a beat despite the multitude of changes and have blooded many of the next generation of players.

Balogun’s debut off the bench was full of emotion, given that three years ago she missed most of the season undergoing chemotherapy treatment for cancer. She afterwards revealed she had been forced to take unpaid leave from her job as a recruitment consultant to be part of the squad this week.

“I thought we were outstanding for the first 13 minutes and then we lost a little bit of control, probably through our own doing,” said Mitchell. “We are having to adapt to changes all the time and so it’s only inevitable, we’ve got a new players, learning new roles, and probably going to take time to learn about how important things like our maul defence are. We’ve got a lot of people new to Test rugby. So yeah, from that perspective, I think we’re doing really well.”

News.title: Middlesbrough manager fumes: ‘Someone decided to go and cheat – it’s a massive advantage’
News.content:
Hello and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s coverage of the EFL Championship play-off semi-final between Middlesbrough and Southampton.

Today’s match was already set to be a huge one but it has now taken even greater significance after a member of Southampton’s analyst team was caught spying on a Middlesbrough training session on Thursday.

The “spy” had professional surveillance equipment, complete with a microphone to record voices and technology to livestream the footage back to someone watching remotely. A brief physical confrontation ensued when a member of Middlesbrough’s media team challenged the man, who refused to identify himself and then ran off.

This morning, our reporter Luke Edwards revealed Southampton have accepted a misconduct charge but claimed the analyst was acting on his own initiative and had not been instructed to travel to Rockcliffe Hall hotel, adjacent to Boro’s training ground, to spy on Kim Hellberg and his players.

While we wait to hear what punishment Southampton receives, there is still a game to play at the Riverside. Speaking before the ‘spygate’ row blew up, Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert said he will not be underestimating the challenge posed by Hellberg’s men despite being on a 19-match league unbeaten run.

“They have been quite clear in the way they approach the game. I think it is quite clear to see where they have their strengths,” Eckert said at a press conference.

“If they catch a good day and they start to flow, I think they are a good team in certain aspects of the game. (But) we come from some good weeks and months. In the end it is about getting our strengths on the pitch like we have been doing for many, many weeks now.”

Southampton reached the play-offs with a fourth-placed finish in the Championship and Boro finished one spot below them on goal difference after both sides secured 80 points.

Stand by for the lineups and build-up to the match!

News.title: Furious Liverpool fans want Slot to go as boos ring out after Chelsea draw
News.content:
By the end of the afternoon, Slot was being asked once again to make the case for him continuing into a third season. When he looks over at Chelsea, now drifting away from the European places in ninth, without a permanent manager and with one point – the one secured at Anfield – from seven games, he may wonder why they could feel confident applauding their fans afterwards. The explanation was that expectations have been driven so low at Chelsea that even a glimmer of fight ahead of next Saturday’s make-or-break FA Cup final was enough for their support on this day.

Does Slot believe he can turn these Liverpool supporters around? “Yeah, I do,” he said. “Not this season, by the way. This season they will have their opinion and it will not change, but if we can have the summer that we are planning to have, I am 100 per cent convinced we will be a different team next season. Different in terms of results, different in how things look. It’s not always that simple because sometimes you know what you have to do but it’s not always possible to get exactly what you want.”

Slot made the argument that Liverpool have injuries. He did not go as far as to say that chief among those missing, Mohamed Salah, seems to be doing his best to suggest that all is not well at the club behind the scenes. In spite of that, this did not present as a manager who feels his position is insecure. It would be typical of FSG to stay the course. The stubbornness of their approach, as well as that of the likes of football chief executive Michael Edwards, has been similarly tested before.

Liverpool had scored through Ryan Gravenberch in the sixth minute, with Ngumoha dominating down the left flank and Chelsea looking very flaky.

Sports.title: Burnley 2 Aston Villa 2: Visitors on track for Champions League football despite Zian Flemming’s equaliser
Sports.content:
NOW that’s what you call coming down to earth with one hell of a bang.

Heroics in Europe on Thursday, hiccups in East Lancashire 72 hours later…against the side with the worst home record in the Prem.





Maybe Aston Villa’s place at the Champions League table is going to come down to a 90-minute final in Istanbul after all.

They went to already-relegated Burnley on the back of thrashing Nottingham Forest to reach a Europa League showdown with Freiburg in a fortnight.

Victory against the Clarets, with just two wins and 15 goals in front of their own fans all season – the worst in the top flight – would have all but booked their place with the Euro big guns ahead of time.

Instead they had to fight all the way for a draw that leaves them just four points ahead of sixth-placed Bournemouth.

With their final two games coming against Liverpool on Friday, then title-chasing Manchester City, Villa have left the door very much ajar for the Cherries.

And this time there can be no excuses because, unlike the fiasco a week earlier, this was no second-string line-up either.



A week before, Unai Emery sent out an all-change line-up which crashed to Spurs. This time there were only three tweaks – but were red-faced once again.

Not due to their own failings either, it should be said. More the spirit and scrapping of a Burnley side determined to bloody a nose or two before they went down.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Led valiantly by stick-at-it striker Zion Flemming, and the magical feet of Hannibal Mejri, Loum Tchaouna and Lesley Ugochukwa.

When the latter two combined for Ugochukwu to hit one from 25 yards, Emi Martinez should have either smothered it or pushed the ball wide.

Instead all he did was knock it back into the danger area, teeing up Jaidon Anthony for the simplest of tap-ins.



It should have been two when Tchaouna picked out Flemming as Ezri Konsa slipped, yet he drove high and wide despite taking deliberate aim.

Villa, for all their neat passing moves, were hardly giving keeper Max Weiss the toughest of work-outs on his Premier League debut.

True, he got away with one when John McGinn fed the ball in but Ross Barkley couldn’t sort out his feet and stabbed wide. He soon made amends.

By the time he did, Villa had already had one would-be equaliser chalked out by VAR after Ollie Watkins nodded in from four yards.

And quite frankly there was no need for the wannabe World Cup striker to stray offside before meeting Morgan Rogers’ cross, either.



Villa had their tails up now, mind, and when Rogers teed up Barkley, his drive had Weiss at full stretch to push behind. He was only delaying the inevitable.

From McGinn’s subsequent corner, Barkley – who had ambled across the box unmarked – rose to flick in a great headed leveller.

And just before the hour Villa were ahead, courtesy of the most route-one goal you will ever see.



Keeper Emi Martinez, never slow to launch an attacking raid, was a yard outside his box when he punted downfield.

His Exocet flew between Axel Tuanzebe and Maxime Esteve, Watkins used his chest to take the pace off it and prodded beneath Weiss.

Game over? Clarets cracked? Job done? Don’t believe a word of it. Burnley may be down, but they were still far from out.

And minutes after Watkins’ strike, Flemming hit the best goal of the game, sidefooting in after a magical flicked ball from Hannibal Mejri.

It would have been the Burnley striker’s second of the game if he’d had longer studs, falling agonisingly short of reaching Hannibal’s earlier low cross.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Back came Villa again, and they certainly had the chances to put their towel on one of the seats at the Champions League table, notably through McGinn.

There remains, of course, the strong likelihood they will get there via the Prem…but don’t rule out having to win the Europa League to make it after this.

Sports.title: Arsenal ace Leandro Trossard seen for first time since wife mysteriously wiped all trace of him from social media
Sports.content:
LEANDRO Trossard has been seen for the first time after The Sun revealed his marriage is in crisis.

The Arsenal ace has been named in the Gunners’ starting 11 to play West Ham United this afternoon – hours after we reported his wife Laura Hilven mysteriously wiped all trace of him from her social media.





Belgian Leandro, 31, was seen in a video posted on Arsenal’s social channels arriving with his teammates at the London Stadium ahead of kick-off at 4.30pm.

The midfielder and Laura, 33, tied the knot in 2019, and would have been a couple for 13 years next month.

However, Laura deleted wedding pictures and has not posted any images wearing her ring since December.

Fellow Belgian Laura has also removed pictures of herself with Trossard posing in Arsenal shirts at the club’s Emirates ­Stadium in North London.

Leandro’s marriage has been under strain while he has been playing a key role in Arsenal’s bid to win the Premier League and Champions League double.

The midfielder is due to line up for the Gunners in a crunch match as they close in on their first title for 22 years.

A source said: “Laura used to have loads of pictures on her Instagram showing her and Leandro on their wedding day, on holidays and going out on date nights, but she has wiped them all.

“If someone looked at her profile now, they would have no clue that they had ever been together, let alone married.”



Blonde Laura previously used her Instagram to showcase their happy life — regularly posting loved-up snaps of them together to her 35,000 followers.

Her now-deleted posts include a snap from Leandro’s proposal in June 2018.

At the time a besotted Laura posted a love heart emoji and gushed online: “I can’t picture my life with anyone other than YOU!



“I SAID YES #hefinallypoppedthequestion #sohappytobeengagedtohim #soonwifey #marriedwiththemanofmydreams.”

On a pic from their wedding day, Laura had written: “I have been told many times, how beautiful it is, how deep it goes.

“But only since I know you I know that love really exists.”

A post from their first wedding anniversary in 2020 showing Laura in a white backless and off-the-shoulder gown, read: “One year down, forever to go!”

And a post showed the pair kissing on a beach in 2020 saw her write: “Myforeverhome.”



There was also a snap from 2022 of the pair holding each other on a beach, with the caption: “Happy 9 years. #iloveyou.”

Laura also removed a picture of the couple wearing Arsenal shirts on the pitch at the Emirates following the team’s final home game of the season last May.

The image was captioned: “Our hearts are RED. Thank you for all the support this season. #LOVEFROMUS.”



Other deleted posts showed the couple enjoying holidays in Ibiza and other sunkissed locations around the world.

Tennis fan Laura also erased any evidence of Trossard’s presence on a hospitality trip to the Wimbledon championships last year — despite him previously appearing in numerous images she posted from their day at the All England Club.

Laura has not posted a picture of herself wearing her wedding or engagement ring since December 5, when she put up a snap of her and three pals with the caption: “Christmas dinner with my ladies.”

In the most recent Instagram image that shows her left hand, posted on March 2, a gold ring can be seen on her middle finger, but her wedding set is missing.

Arsenal play West Ham today in a crucial Premier League game as they battle Man City for the title.



If Arsenal win their last three matches of the season they will be Premier League champions for the first time since 2004.

The team are also riding high in Europe after an unbeaten run to reach the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest on May 30.

Looking ahead to the final, Trossard said: “We will be ready for it. In one game, everything can happen.”



Leandro moved to England with Laura after winning the Belgian league title with Genk in 2019.

He joined Brighton and Hove Albion where he spent four years — scoring 25 goals in 116 games.

But his career got a huge boost in January 2023 when Arsenal signed him in a £27million deal.

He has played 121 times for the Gunners and scored 26 goals.

Leandro also made his debut for Belgium in 2020.



He played for his country in the 2022 World Cup and the Euro 2020 and 2024 tournaments, and is looking forward to the World Cup in the US, Canada and Mexico.

Earlier this year Trossard sustained a hip injury which caused him to miss games, and on his return to action he appeared to be struggling for form.

But over the past few weeks he has again become a regular starter in the Arsenal team, including against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League semi-final second leg last Tuesday.

Laura has been a regular spectator at Arsenal games since Trossard signed for the club.



She has shared pictures on Instagram of her watching in the stands along with Bukayo Saka’s girlfriend Tolami Benson and Kai Havertz’s wife Sophia.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She is also pals with comedian Matt Lucas, who is an Arsenal fan.

He attended her 33rd birthday party in October.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest 1 Newcastle 1: Elliot Anderson scores emotional equaliser against former club in huge survival boost
Sports.content:
“CAN the season just end already?” grumbled a Forest fan walking past me, leaving the City Ground five minutes from time.

He will have missed Elliot Anderson‘s 88th-minute equaliser to snatch a point against Newcastle, which could be vital in securing the Tricky Trees’ Premier League status for next season.



His mood was reflected by most of the Midlands crowd until their heroic number eight stepped up at the death, with a goal that pretty much condemned Newcastle to mid-table obscurity.



Just a week ago, Newcastle could still have played in the Champions League or, equally, been playing Championship football next season.

Now it looks likely they won’t do either.

The visitors thought it was won when substitutes Jacob Ramsey and Harvey Barnes combined for the latter to give them the lead after 74 minutes.

They seemed to be hitting form at just the right time, had leapfrogged Sunderland in the table on goal difference, and would still be in with a great chance of playing in Europe next season.

But a few shirtless Geordies pulled their black and white tops back on when Anderson’s finish moved them back below their local rivals in the table, albeit still with a good chance of winning their next two and overtaking the Black Cats again.

A change in shape for Forest, to play with five defenders, saw the visitors start the sharper of the two sides.

And Eddie Howe‘s men could have had the lead within 11 minutes, when Will Osula’s early volley was misdirected wide of the post.

Dilane Bakwa danced through the Newcastle defence and bent a shot goalwards five minutes later, only for it to meet the head of Lewis Hall and be turned away for a corner that amounted to nothing.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The first half was in danger of petering out, which saw both sides ramp up the pressure.



Sandro Tonali and Anderson battled it out in midfield, both of whom have been linked with moves to a host of other Premier League clubs in the summer.

But Anderson’s effort from range fell well wide of the post, and Tonali’s is still floating down the River Trent.

Bakwa was the one causing most of the problems for the Newcastle defence, as his deep cross led to Forest’s best chance of the half, with Nick Pope forced to react quickly to a Taiwo Awoniyi header and a Jair Cunha shot in quick succession.

Newcastle attempted to play on the counter, firing balls into Nick Woltemade and asking him to create for the others.

Osula had another chance to open the scoring before half-time from Woltemade’s pass, and should’ve scored, but Matz Sels was out quickly to close down the angle for his low shot.



The half-time whistle left both sides frustrated at a lack of quality in the final third.

And fans were fairly unenthused about a finely-poised second half, despite the techno music that blared as Forest came out for the second 45.

The second half started how the first ended – slowly.

More long-range efforts and poorly-weighted passes missed their intended targets, from two groups of players who looked tired of playing football altogether.

Awoniyi was the first Forest player to see a sight of goal in the second half, but his lacklustre effort was stopped by Sels after he shrugged off any defenders that dared come near him.



Howe turned to Ramsey and Barnes with half an hour to go, bringing the end to disappointing a day for Woltemade and Jacob Murphy.

When Woltemade scored from the spot in the reverse fixture, his signing seemed money well spent in a bid to replace Alexander Isak as he bagged his fourth goal in five starts since his club-record £69million move from Stuttgart.

When he left the pitch in this one, Newcastle immediately looked like a better side.

Fans were shocked when they didn’t open the scoring just two minutes later, after two brilliant chances fell to captain Bruno Guimaraes.

His first opening came inside the penalty area, as a result of a poor clearance from Morato, but he scuffed his effort straight at Sels.



Following a smart darting run into the box, Guimaraes tried to fire a strike across goal, but Sels was down to make another stop.

And to make it a hat-trick of close calls for Newcastle in a matter of minutes, Osula struck the crossbar with a venomous free-kick from range.

Eventually, Newcastle’s dominance paid off when Ramsey held off Morato under pressure before feeding Barnes, who lifted the ball over an onrushing Sels.

Forest pushed for a leveller with the introduction of James McAtee and big man Lorenzo Lucca, and finally found it through Anderson, who got his reward for battling like a madman in midfield throughout.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He showed exactly why his former club shouldn’t have sold him for the sake of PSR, when he smashed a left-footed effort past Pope from an awkward angle and wheeled off to celebrate with a group of fans who adore him.



A spur of motivation saw them then look for a winner, but one couldn’t be found for Forest, who will battle for their place in the Premier League again next weekend against Manchester United.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace 2 Everton 2: Jean-Philippe Mateta dents Toffees’ European dream as hosts twice fight back from behind
Sports.content:
JEAN-PHILIPPE MATETA kept the Euro party going at Crystal Palace with a late leveller.

The colourful Frenchman scored Palace’s second equaliser of the day then led the Selhurst Park orchestra as the fans sang about the impending journey to Germany for the Conference League final later this month.





It is clear where the supporters’ priorities lie and understandably so, as this point all but guarantees Premier League safety for another season.

All roads lead to Leipzig for the Palace ultras and the players as they focus on a significant European trophy when they face Rayo Vallecano on May 27.

It is an ambition that Everton have been quietly working on in the past few weeks but twice blowing the lead will make that dream all the more difficult to achieve now.

David Moyes’ team sit 10th and still within touching distance of European qualification but tossing away three points after twice taking the lead has dealt them a big blow.

Captain James Tarkowski put the visitors one up after only six minutes when he latched onto a corner that appeared to be inadvertently flicked on by Jaydee Canvot.

It still needed a decisive touch to plant the ball over the line and give Everton a dream start at a tough ground for visiting teams.



Palace have not lost on home turf since February 11 – a run of nine games that includes last Thursday’s 2-1 victory over Shakhtar Donetsk that is sending them to the Conference League final two weeks on Wednesday.

The Eagles’ sluggish start was understandable as they strive to put the prospect of a big European final to one side while shuffling towards the end of the domestic season and the climax to Oliver Glasner’s reign as boss.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS



Even so, Selhurst Park is an awkward venue and despite being under the cosh, Palace managed to eke out an equaliser on 34 minutes.

Ismaila Sarr’s 12th goal since February 1 had a touch of fortune in the run up with his first-time shot deflecting off the boot of Everton defender Michael Keane straight back to him.

But with a second bite at the cherry the forward made no mistake and buried the ball beyond England keeper Jordan Pickford.

Everton have been suffering late collapses recently, defeats to Liverpool and West Ham being prime examples.

Moyes has clearly been working on it and demanding his team get in early and land the first blow.



Having taken the lead on six minutes then been pegged back, Everton regained the advantage less than 120 seconds into the second half.

The clearance upfield from Tarkowski looked route one but the football from striker Beto to finish the job was sublime with strength to hold off Maxence Lacroix.

That was before shimmying past the Palace defender inside the six-yard box then delivering a low shot through the legs of keeper Dean Henderson.

Mateta came off the bench to replace Jorgen Strand Larsen on 65 minutes and only seven minutes later smashed the ball into the back of the net with a rising shot.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The charismatic centre-forward then whipped up the crowd by acting as band leader getting the fans to raise their voices and put pressure on Everton.



Both sides upped the tempo in the closing stages with Everton’s Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Palace’s Adam Wharton hitting the woodwork inside the final ten minutes.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho breaks silence on Real Madrid manager links with Chelsea legend wanted by former club
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO has addressed the rumours heavily linking him to former club Real Madrid.

He could be set for a return to the Spanish capital in what would be a dramatic return for the Portuguese star.





But he says any club that wants him will have just a week to get it done once the season is over.

The Portuguese legend still has a year left on the Benfica contract he signed last summer, so Real Madrid bosses might have to persuade their former man once more.

In Sunday’s press conference ahead of their clash with Braga tomorrow, the Special One said “for the moment” he hasn’t heard from anyone at Madrid.

He said: “There is something I would like to emphasise, in the world of football, it is not the managers who are interested in going or not going.

“When something happens, it is the clubs that are interested and that initiate the procedures to get the people they want.”

He continued: “People keep talking about Real Madrid, and I’m still avoiding that, honestly. I haven’t had any contact with the president or any other club official.

“In the final stages of the season, I don’t speak to anyone. I haven’t had any contact with Real Madrid, and I won’t have any until the last league match against Estoril.

“Then there is a one-week window, in which I will be free to speak to whoever I think I should speak to, but until then, everything that has come out of meetings and calls is speculation.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

So despite breaking the silence on the rumours Mourinho still seems to be tight-lipped on the whole situation – it would make sense if it was out of respect for his current club Benfica.

He quashed rumours linking him to the club at the beginning of the month and it seems that fans will have to wait until the end of the season to find out where the former Chelsea manager will be.

After the sacking of Liam Rosenior the Blues have also been linked to the fan-favourite.

Mourinho won three Premier League titles across two spells at Stamford Bridge – he went back-to-back in 2005 and 2006 before taking Chelsea back to the top in the second season of his returning spell in 2015.



He made his fairytale return to Chelsea after three seasons at Real Madrid in which he brought the LaLiga title back into the hands of Los Blancos after four years without it in 2012.

If the rumours turn out to be true and Mourinho becomes Real Madrid’s manager, Madridistas will be hoping he can work the miracles that he did back in 2012, as bitter rivals Barcelona look all but set to maintain their crown.

Barca host Real Madrid tonight in El Clasico, needing just a point to confirm the league title – they’re 11 points clear with four games to go.

Sports.title: Fire breaks out at major 50,000-capacity European football stadium during match as emergency services rush to scene
Sports.content:
A FIRE broke out in worrying scenes at Sweden’s national team stadium as fans evacuated.

AIK hosted Djurgardens at the 50,000-capacity Strawberry Arena in Stockholm on Sunday.





The visitors led 2-1 after an action-packed start to their Allsvenskan league derby clash.

But with 25 minutes on the clock, the referee stopped play and the players headed off the pitch because of the fire in the stands – although they remained outside and did not return to the changing rooms.

It is unclear what triggered the blaze.

However, it possibly started due to flares inside the ground.



TV cameras quickly cut to the drama as fans cleared out of the way while the flames roared.

Dramatic photos then showed huge clouds of smoke billowing from the fire across the pitch.

Firefighters immediately rushed to the scene.

They used hoses to control the blaze and put it out as other security personnel kept supporters away from the danger.

AIK’s head of security Henrik Koch confirmed the fire was put out without anyone being hurt.

Koch said: “No injuries occurred and the fire was extinguished.”



The match restarted after a few minutes.

Following the stoppage, Djurgardens added a third in first-half injury time.

However, there was another delay early in the second half when the home fans set off more flares.



This time, the players were taken off the field for an emergency meeting before the game resumed.

Sports.title: How Arsenal are using AI-generated song to propel them to historic Premier League and Champions League Double
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are using AI to push them over the line in their bid for a historic Champions League and Premier League Double – but not in the way people might expect.

The Gunners aren’t using the tech to research opponents or deep-dive into their own data, but instead have been listening to an unusual AI-generated song to inspire them to silverware.





At the full-time whistle on Tuesday night, as Arsenal secured a spot in the Champions League final with victory over Atletico Madrid, the Emirates crowd roared into a party atmosphere.

The players were celebrating on the pitch as the PA system blared out music – including the AI-generated tune that has been the soundtrack to Arsenal’s recent success.

Manager Mikel Arteta could be seen dancing to the song alongside Leandro Trossard, while the players were all beaming from ear to ear as they sang along to the words.

It was also played in the dressing room during the post-match celebrations on Tuesday.

The song, which doesn’t appear to have an official name, simply recites the names of the players in the Arsenal squad to the backdrop of a catchy beat.

It also features terms like “connection”, “make it happen” and “North London Forever” – phrases that have regularly been used by Arteta.

Arteta has already used the song to inspire his team, playing it in the background of training sessions in recent weeks.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



But there is no trace of where the song originated from, with nobody publicly claiming it as their own.

Asked about how the song became a part of the team’s celebrations, Arteta said: “It came there, somehow. The players really like it.”

The Gunners boss also admitted that he “loves it” and even agreed that it has become the soundtrack of Arsenal’s season.

It was Arteta who orchestrated the addition of North London Forever to Arsenal’s pre-match routine earlier in his reign at the Emirates.

Once a controversial addition, the club anthem – which was adopted after it was released by Arsenal fan Louis Dunford – is now part of every home game.



The Spaniard has also used music as part of his training sessions, playing You’ll Never Walk Alone before Liverpool games and blasting Brazilian samba music to try and unlock his free-flowing attack.

Arteta has already used a host of innovative techniques to inspire his squad this season as he looks to finally end their run of three consecutive second-place finishes.

Training exercises have included players dribbling a ball while avoiding dropping pens held between their fingers, and standing in a circle holding hands to feel connected.

Other techniques during his Arsenal tenure included using a light bulb as part of his team talk and hiring pickpockets to steal players’ belongings in a meeting.

Arteta recently revealed that he chooses a different theme for each match to keep his side motivated and singing from the same hymn sheet.



With so many different nationalities in the Arsenal squad, Arteta emphasises ensuring his message can be understood by all.

Sports.title: Hansi Flick's father dies hours before El Clasico as Barcelona release statement
Sports.content:
Hansi Flick's father dies hours before El Clasico as Barcelona release statement

Barcelona announced the death of Hansi Flick's father on Sunday afternoon, with their head coach still expected to be in the dugout for their clash with Real Madrid

View Image Barcelona announced the death of Hansi Flick's father on Sunday (Image: Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

Hansi Flick will take charge of Barcelona in the El Clasico on Sunday evening despite the death of his father being announced on the day of the game.

‌



A statement shared by the Spanish champions confirmed that the 61-year-old's father had passed away. "FC Barcelona and the entire blaugrana family wish to send all our love to Hansi Flick after the passing of his father," the statement read.

‌



"We share in your sorrow and our thoughts are with you and your family during this difficult time."

‌



Flick is expected to be in the dugout for the match with Real Madrid, where both clubs will pay tribute to his father by wearing black armbands. A minute's silence will also be held before the game.

Barca's rivals showed class by sharing their condolences to Flick with a statement of their own, which read: "Real Madrid, its president and its directors deeply regret the death of the father of Hansi Flick.

‌



"Real Madrid wants to express its condolences and affection to their families and all their loved ones. Rest in peace."

Barcelona will clinch back-to-back La Liga titles with either a win or a draw against Real Madrid at the Nou Camp.

Flick has won four trophies with Barca since being chosen as Xavi's successor by the Spanish giants back in the summer of 2024.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe to miss El Clasico after 'walking out of training' amid Real Madrid chaos
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe to miss El Clasico after 'walking out of training' amid Real Madrid chaos

Real Madrid will take on Barcelona minus Kylian Mbappe after their star striker felt a muscle issue in training and called time on his session - leaving Los Blancos light in attack

View 2 Images Kylian Mbappe will miss Real Madrid's game at Barcelona

Kylian Mbappe will miss Sunday night's El Clasico after the Real Madrid star left the training pitch on Saturday - citing discomfort in his hamstring.

‌



The Frenchman has been in the headlines for all the wrong reasons recently as millions sign a petition calling for him to keep booted out of the club. Real's season looks set to end without a trophy whilst Barcelona are closing in on another La Liga title.

‌



Real could at least get one over on their rivals at the Nou Camp, but if they are to do so then Marca claims they will have to do it without their World Cup winner. The 27-year-old stunned his team-mates by pulling up during training, announcing his issue and walking off. Los Blancos have released their squad list for the heavyweight clash tonight, but it only included four forwards, none of which are Mbappe. It leaves Vinicius Jnr as their leading light in attack.

‌



Mbappe has been the subject of widespread criticism from the Bernabeu supporters after he chose to go on a yacht holiday with his new girlfriend while recovering from his hamstring injury. The petition calling for the club to sell him this summer has landed a staggering 70millions of signatures.

Jose Mourinho backed to return to Chelsea AGAIN amid Real Madrid talks READ MORE :

Mbappe has scored 41 goals in all competitions this term and found the net for the opening goal when Real beat Barcelona 2-1 earlier this season. However a recent blip has seen them win only five of their last ten La Liga games.

‌



The Spanish giants come into the Clasico following a bust up involving Federico Valverde and Aurélien Tchouaméni. The duo were involved in a shocking dressing room row with the Uruguayan left with a cut his head and needing hospital treatment. Both players were fined €500,000 for their roles in the controversy.

View 2 Images Real Madrid have already dealt with a controversy involving Aurelien Tchouameni and Federico Valverde (Image: Europa Press Sports, Europa Press via Getty Images)

Alvaro Arbeloa, who is set to be moved on in the summer, said: “Valverde and Tchouameni deserve for us to move on, to give them a chance to keep fighting for this club. I’m very proud of them. I won’t allow this to be used to question their professionalism."

Article continues below

The Real boss also hit out at the leak from within the club. “The most serious thing for me, what hurts me most, is that what happens in the Real Madrid dressing room should stay there,” he added. “If things that happen in the dressing room are leaked, I think it’s a betrayal of Real Madrid and what this badge represents."

Sports.title: Kieran McKenna 'likely to leave' Ipswich Town for new job despite promotion
Sports.content:
Kieran McKenna 'likely to leave' Ipswich Town for new job despite promotion

Kieran McKenna helped Ipswich Town clinch an automatic return to the Premier League following relegation but it remains to be seen if he will still be in charge next season

View 2 Images Ipswich Town may struggle to keep hold of Kieran McKenna this summer (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

Ipswich Town could lose their highly-rated head coach Kieran McKenna this summer with the Northern Irishman said to be 'increasingly likely' to leave Portman Road for a new job.

‌



McKenna has been a revelation in his first managerial role with Ipswich, overseeing three promotions in four years, including an instant return to the Premier League this season following relegation last term. The 39-year-old's accomplishments in Suffolk have not gone unnoticed, however, with McKenna regularly touted with other top-flight jobs.

‌



After guiding Ipswich to the Premier League for the first time following successive promotions two years ago, McKenna was considered for a number of top roles, including the vacancy at his former club, Manchester United.

‌



He eventually stayed to lead Ipswich in the Premier League before remaining in the role to respond to relegation with a promotion campaign this year. But a new report has cast doubt on the likelihood of McKenna staying on at Portman Road this time around.

The Sun claim that McKenna is expected to leave if he receives an offer from a rival Premier League club this summer, with Ipswich even 'drawing up' a shortlist of potential successors.

Crystal Palace are among those who may move for McKenna as they prepare to appoint a new head coach to replace the outgoing Oliver Glasner.

‌



The Eagles are understood to have identified Andoni Iraola as their top target to take over. But the sought-after Bournemouth boss also has interest from Chelsea with Palace likely to turn their attention to McKenna if Iraola proves to be unattainable.

View 2 Images McKenna guided Ipswich Town to promotion this season (Image: Nigel French/PA Wire)

Fulham could also come into the equation for McKenna amid the ongoing uncertainty over the future of Marco Silva. He, too, is admired by Chelsea and out of contract at the end of the season, with no agreement currently in place for him to continue at Craven Cottage.

‌



McKenna signed a four-year contract with Ipswich back in 2024 after winning promotion to the Premier League. Those terms include a significant compensation figure, thought to be around £5million, which means poaching him would not be cheap for any club.

Ipswich, who were languishing in League One when McKenna took charge, clinched promotion to the Premier League on the final day of the Championship season with a comprehensive 3-0 win over QPR.

Sports.content:
Championship star awkwardly forgets his wife's birthday as he chases Premier League glory

The Middlesbrough defender Callum Brittain had been too focused on the crucial Championship play‑off tie against Southampton

View 3 Images Callum Brittain ended up forgetting his wife's birthday amid Boro's play‑off push (Image: Greig Cowie/Shutterstock)

Middlesbrough star Callum Brittain has been so focused on his side's play‑off push that he even forgot his wife's birthday. His partner, Bethany revealed on social media that the occasion completely slipped his mind.

‌



Brittain featured the entire 90 minutes in the goalless draw against Southampton at the Riverside Stadium. A decision will be taken to the second leg of the play-off set to take place on Tuesday (May 12, 8pm).

‌



Boro dominated the first half but couldn't take their chances which was a familiar story in the second half of the season. Tommy Conway came closest when he struck the post.

‌



Southampton boss storms out press conference as Middlesbrough manager blasts 'cheats' READ MORE :

Saints took control in the second half, as Boro were unable to keep the ball or pin their opponents back as effectively. The visitors almost won it twice in the final five minutes, but ultimately, it's still all to play for on the south coast.

As expected before the clash, Brittain knuckled down and entered full focus mode, leaving Bethany to laugh off the forgotten birthday.

Taking to Instagram, she wrote: "If any Boro fans were worried about his level of focus, he actually forgot my birthday this morning xxx. UTFB," followed by laughing and heart emojis.

‌



View 3 Images Bethany's message on social media

Meanwhile, the defender, a regular starter under Kim Hellberg, took to Instagram afterwards - only to be reminded once again by fans about the awkward moment.

"What an incredible atmosphere! Lost for words today, inspiring support and an amazing experience, thank you Boro fans," he wrote in a post. "The boys run themselves into the ground today and we’ll do the exact same Tuesday! UTFB."

‌

‌

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney makes Premier League title prediction before Arsenal's response - 'I feel'
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney makes Premier League title prediction before Arsenal's response - 'I feel'

Arsenal and Manchester City have nine points left to play for in the Premier League title race and former England striker Wayne Rooney has given his verdict on the battle

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney has weighed in on the title run‑ins of Manchester City and Arsenal

Wayne Rooney reckons neither Arsenal nor Manchester City will drop points between now and the final whistle of the season - a outcome that would see Mikel Arteta's men clinch the Premier League title by just two points. The Gunners must bounce back from City's emphatic 3-0 victory over Brentford on Saturday when they take on West Ham at the London Stadium.

‌



Arsenal can take another massive stride towards the Premier League crown despite City refusing to let go of the race. Goals from Jeremy Doku, Erling Haaland and Omar Marmoush wrapped up the win that hauled Pep Guardiola's men to within two points of the north Londoners.

‌



City still have nine points left to fight for, including a game in hand against Crystal Palace, scheduled for Wednesday (May 13th). Arsenal equally have nine points remaining to play for, kicking off with their trip to the Hammers.

‌



OPINION Andy Dunn Arsenal can begin title party at West Ham and put celebration police on alert

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Following that fixture, they face Burnley at the Emirates before rounding off their league campaign against Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park, ahead of the Champions League final showdown with Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest on May 30. City, meanwhile, must navigate the FA Cup final against Chelsea before their last two league outings - away at Bournemouth and at home to Aston Villa at the Etihad Stadium, reports Football London.

‌



Speaking on Match of the Day, Rooney weighed up both teams' remaining schedules, concluding that each side looks set to win every one of their outstanding fixtures.

"I think City just have to try and win their games, I said this last week that I felt City would drop points against Everton," Rooney said. "I feel both teams will win every game [from now], which makes Arsenal champions."

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta and Pep Guardiola are in a straight race for the Premier League title

‌



When questioned about what the Arsenal squad might be feeling ahead of a possible title triumph, Rooney explained: "Excitement, nervous. You get every emotion and obviously with Man City winning today, now it's on Arsenal to go out and win the game against West Ham.

"Every type of emotion you think you can have, you go through over this next couple of weeks and it's brilliant when you're in it and when you get out of it at the right time then it's such a good feeling. But when you're on the wrong side of it, it's one of the worst feelings in the world."

Should both sides claim victory in their remaining fixtures, Arsenal would conclude the season on 85 points with City finishing on 83.

Sports.title: 'World's most beautiful football stadium' faces ban as club could have to move 150 miles
Sports.content:
'World's most beautiful football stadium' faces ban as club could have to move 150 miles

This football club potentially face moving their home games across the country from their picturesque stadium should they qualify for Europe

View 3 Images Como could run into issues if they clinch European football (Image: Getty Images)

Serie A side Como may be forced to play away from their stadium if they clinch qualification for European football. The Italian side have secured their passage into the Conference League next season after defeating Hellas Verona on Sunday.

‌



It's been a stellar season for the minnows, who are managed by ex-Arsenal and Chelsea star Cesc Fabregas. Competing in Europe would be quite the achievement for a club that was in the second division in 2024.

‌



However, such success could result in logistical issues due to their stunning Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium not meeting UEFA regulations. The ground, which is on the shores of Lake Como, has been described by some as the "world's most beautiful stadium."

‌



Having opened in 1927, it underwent renovations in order to meet the legal standards required for the Italian top-flight. Inspectors visited the stadium in April in order to assess its suitability for European competition.

They raised the problem of the temporary scaffold curve, with the stand being the location of the club's ultras, but UEFA rules mean Como must permanently fix the issue.

Man City's new stadium name explained as big change made before Brentford clash READ MORE :

Casemiro injury means Man Utd star cannot trigger £375k-a-week contract clause READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The regulations state that "stands must be fixed to a load-bearing foundation and may not be based on or contain any tubular/scaffolding structures." Club president Mirwan Suwaso has been given support by Como's mayor to build a permanent structure this summer.

Not only will the pitch need to be widened from 66 metres to UEFA's required 68m, but a two-metre buffer will have to be created between the touchline and advertising boards.

View 3 Images The Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium has a capacity of 13,602 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



A resolution with residents will need to be settled, with locals worried about the effects European competition will have on increased traffic and road infrastructure. Should the work not be completed in time for a European campaign next season, Como will need to find an alternative stadium.

Among the potential grounds touted are Sassuolo's Mapei Stadium, which is a staggering 150 miles away from Como. Udinese's Bluenergy Stadium has also been proposed as an alternate option.

View 3 Images Cesc Fabregas has established himself as one of Europe's most promising managers at Como (Image: Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Article continues below

The iconic San Siro, which is joint-owned by AC Milan and Inter Milan, will not be able to be used by Como due to the scheduling issues that would arise by three clubs using the same stadium.

Fabregas has managed Como since 2024 and even possesses a financial stake in the club. Given the progress he's made as a manager, the former Spain international has already been linked to Premier League jobs, with some touting him as a future replacement for Mikel Arteta at Arsenal.

Sports.title: Wardley's trainer explains decision not to throw in towel in Dubois loss
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley's trainer explained his decision not to throw in the towel during his fighter's punishing loss to Daniel Dubois in their world heavyweight title fight.

Dubois was crowned as the new WBO champion after climbing off the canvas twice to stop Wardley in the 11th round of a brutal all-British clash in Manchester on Saturday night.

In social media posts on Sunday, Wardley's trainer firstly confirmed that "most importantly Fabio is OK" and then revealed why he did not halt the fight himself before referee Howard Foster waved it off.

Ben Davison wrote: "On last night - Firstly congrats to Dubois.

"Two tremendous warriors in a modern-day classic. We are super proud of Fabio.

"I actually agree the fight could [have] been stopped earlier.

"I did not see Fabio stumble before walking over to the doctor at the start of round 10 as ironically we were discussing with each other to 'have the towel in hand' by which time he had gone over and seen the doctor and seemed much steadier on his legs which is what we saw.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Daniel Dubois had nothing but praise for Fabio Wardley following their sensational fight at the Co-op Live Arena in Manchester for the WBO heavyweight belt.

"It's such a difficult job to not only find a balance but to strike at the right time to stop a fight like that on a whim when your guy is responsive and firing back.

"I've been praised for not towelling Fury (Wilder). I was praised for not towelling Wood (Conlan). I was firstly criticised then later praised for towelling Wood (Lara).

"Two occasions we looked at it but one, the end of the round came [and] two, Fabio fired back and killed Dubois' momentum. Again very difficult in the circumstances of the fighter being responsive and firing back.

"I've seen mixed opinions on this one but I agree it COULD [have] been stopped earlier. However, with that said I think Howard Foster got it bang on from his terms."

Image: Fabio Wardley's face was bloodied and swollen by the time the fight was stopped

On Wardley, Davison said: "Very easy to forget what Fabio has achieved.

"From four white collar fights to heavyweight champion of the world. Not an easy task to do or for us to help guide against the best in the world.

"Never been done before, never be done again."
